'''Nikos K. Logothetis''' ({{langx|el|Νίκος Λογοθέτης}}; born 5 November 1950 in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]]) is a Greek [[biologist]] and [[neuroscientist]]. Logothetis studies [[visual perception]] and [[Object recognition (cognitive science)|object recognition]] and is best known for his work demonstrating that [[Blood-oxygen-level-dependent imaging|BOLD]] [[Functional magnetic resonance imaging|fMRI]] data correlate with neuronal activity.<ref name="lancet01">{{cite journal |title=Neuroscientists take a BOLD step forward |last=Butcher |first=James |date=2001-07-14 |journal=The Lancet |volume=358 |issue=9276 |page=128 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(01)05383-1|s2cid=54368004 }}</ref> From 1996 to 2022 Logothetis directed the Department of Physiology of Cognitive Processes at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics]] in [[Tübingen]]. Since 2021 he has served as director of the International Center for Primate Brain Research (ICPBR) in [[Shanghai]], where he co-directs research alongside Chinese neuroscientist [[Mu-ming Poo]].<ref name="sci20">{{cite journal|last=Vogel |first=Gretchen |title=Animal rights conflict prompts leading researcher to leave Germany for China |date=2020-01-27 |journal=Science |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/animal-rights-conflict-prompts-leading-researcher-leave-germany-china |doi=10.1126/science.abb0626 |s2cid=214253067 |access-date=2020-01-27}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
In the 1970s, Logothetis studied piano at the [[Hellenic Observatory of Athens|Hellenic Conservatory of Athens]] under Georgios Platon, a composer and principal pianist of the [[Greek National Opera]].<ref name=":1" /> He was also a founding member of the rock band PeLoMa BoKiou, whose name derived from the surnames of its members: Nikos Daperis, Nikos Logothetis, Takis Marinakis, [[Vlassis Bonatsos]], and Yiannis Kiourtzoglou. Their debut single, "Γαρύφαλλε, Γαρύφαλλε" (Carnation, Carnation), later included on an album, remains well-regarded for its lyrics and emotive quality. The band performed progressive rock, occasionally drawing comparison to Carlos Santana's style, and was regarded as one of Greece's prominent rock groups.<ref name=":1" />

Logothetis received a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in mathematics from the [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens]] and a bachelor's degree in biology from the [[Aristotle University of Thessaloniki]]. He completed doctoral studies at [[LMU Munich]] under the supervision of [[Ernst Pöppel]], receiving a PhD in human neurobiology in 1985.<ref name="mpg">{{cite web |url=https://www.mpg.de/390847/biologische_kybernetik_wissM1 |title=Prof. Dr. Nikos K. Logothetis |website=Max-Planck Gesellschaft |access-date=2020-01-27}}</ref>

== Career ==
Logothetis moved to the United States to take up a postdoctoral fellowship in the Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he subsequently became a research scientist.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=LOGOTHETIS Nikos--International Center For Primate Brain Research |url=https://www.icpbr.ac.cn/lab/logothetis/people/202307/t20230712_170621.html |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=www.icpbr.ac.cn |language=en}}</ref> In 1990, he joined the faculty of the Division of Neuroscience at [[Baylor College of Medicine]] in Houston, Texas, where his research focused on the neurophysiological mechanisms of visual perception and object recognition in the [[macaque]] [[inferior temporal cortex]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Nikos Logothetis from Center for Excellence in Brain Science and Intelligence Technology Awarded CAS International Science and Technology Cooperation Award |url=http://english.cebsit.cas.cn/News/ComprehensiveNews/2019Year/202601/t20260130_1147669.html |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=english.cebsit.cas.cn}}</ref>

In 1996, Logothetis was appointed Scientific Member of the [[Max Planck Society]] and director at the Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics in Tübingen, where, in 1997, he established the Department of Physiology of Cognitive Processes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nikos K. Logothetis |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/nikos-k-logothetis-hsavtz/ |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=National Academy of Science |language=en-US}}</ref> There, he led a research programme combining single- and multi-unit [[electrophysiology]] with [[functional magnetic resonance imaging]] (fMRI), initially in non-human primates and later extended to rodents. This work led to the establishment of the institute's Magnetic Resonance Center.<ref name="kybfac">{{cite web |url=http://www.kyb.mpg.de/nc/employee/details/nikos.html#=2 |title=Prof. Dr. Nikos Logothetis |website=Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics |publisher=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft|access-date=2020-01-27}}</ref>

Since 2021, Logothetis has served as co-director and senior investigator of the International Center for Primate Brain Research (ICPBR) in Shanghai, an institute affiliated with the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] and established to conduct large-scale non-human primate research.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2020-01-27 |title=World renowned neuroscientist and animal researcher, Nikos Logothetis, moves to China |url=https://speakingofresearch.com/2020/01/27/world-renowned-neuroscientist-and-animal-researcher-nikos-logothetis-moves-to-china/ |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=Speaking of Research |language=en}}</ref> He co-directs the center with neuroscientist [[Mu-ming Poo]], scientific director of the CAS Center for Excellence in Brain Science and Intelligence Technology.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Greek Leading researcher Nikos Logothetis stops experiments in monkeys – EUSJA |url=https://www.eusja.org/leading-greek-researcher-nikos-logothetis-stops-experiments-in-monkeys/ |access-date=2026-06-28 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-19 |title='China is in a good phase': award-winning neuroscientist on why he left Europe |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3291474/russia-rewards-top-neuroscientist-who-left-europe-china-vyzov-prize |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}}</ref>

He is a member of the editorial board for ''[[Current Biology]]''.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.cell.com/current-biology/editorial-board | title=Cell Press: Current Biology}}</ref>

Logothetis is one of the 2003 winners of the [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]].<ref>[https://www.jeantet.ch/en/prix-louis-jeantet/laureats/2003-en/professeur-nikos-k-logothetis/ Louis-Jeantet Prize]</ref>

== Research ==
According to Logothetis, in order to understand a system, a description of it is necessary at all levels. As a result,  intracortical cell recording and also modeling and [[Medical imaging|imaging]] is conducted at all levels in his department. Therefore, in addition to [[functional MRI|functional magnetic resonance imaging]], 'in vivo' [[spectroscopy]] is also used, and the working group is researching smart contrast agents (SCA) in order to make functional imaging useful for effects other than [[haemodynamics|haemodynamic response]].<ref name="lancet01" /><ref name="sci20" />

From the late 1980s, Logothetis studied the neural basis of visual awareness in macaques using [[binocular rivalry]], in which conflicting images shown to each eye produce an alternating rather than fused percept. With Jeffrey Schall, he found that some neurons in the [[Middle temporal area|middle temporal visual area]] (MT/V5) tracked the monkey's perceptual reports rather than the fixed retinal stimulus.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Perceptual changes - a key to our consciousness |url=https://www.mpg.de/620968/pressRelease20101118 |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=www.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Single neuron consciousness in the binocular brain |url=https://medicalxpress.com/news/2018-06-neuron-consciousness-binocular-brain.html |website=Medical Xpress}}</ref> A 1996 study with David Leopold showed that early visual areas such as [[Visual cortex|V1]] correlated only weakly with perceptual switches, whereas higher-order [[ventral stream]] neurons, especially in [[Inferior temporal cortex|inferior temporal (IT) cortex]], closely tracked what the animal perceived. These findings led him to argue that neural correlates of awareness become more prevalent at later stages of the visual hierarchy. With [[Randolph Blake]], he later proposed that rivalry reflects competition at multiple levels of the visual system rather than a single site.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blake |first1=Randolph |last2=Logothetis |first2=Nikos K. |date=2002 |title=Visual competition |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nrn701 |journal=Nature Reviews Neuroscience |language=en |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=13–21 |doi=10.1038/nrn701 |pmid=11823801 |issn=1471-0048|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1999, with Max Planck colleagues, he produced some of the first functional images of the monkey brain using high-field MRI, validating fMRI for primate neuroscience.<ref name=":0" /> A 2001 ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' paper then reported the first simultaneous intracortical electrophysiology and fMRI from monkey visual cortex.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Logothetis |first1=Nikos K. |last2=Guggenberger |first2=Heinz |last3=Peled |first3=Sharon |last4=Pauls |first4=Jon |date=1999 |title=Functional imaging of the monkey brain |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nn0699_555 |journal=Nature Neuroscience |language=en |volume=2 |issue=6 |pages=555–562 |doi=10.1038/9210 |pmid=10448221 |issn=1546-1726|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Comparing [[Local field potential|local field potentials]] (LFPs) and spiking activity with the BOLD signal, the study found that LFPs, reflecting synaptic input and local processing rather than a region's spiking output, best predicted the haemodynamic response, indicating that BOLD signals reflect input to and processing within a brain area more than its output to other regions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Logothetis |first1=Nikos K. |last2=Pauls |first2=Jon |last3=Augath |first3=Mark |last4=Trinath |first4=Torsten |last5=Oeltermann |first5=Axel |date=2001 |title=Neurophysiological investigation of the basis of the fMRI signal |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35084005 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=412 |issue=6843 |pages=150–157 |doi=10.1038/35084005 |pmid=11449264 |bibcode=2001Natur.412..150L |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This conclusion strongly shaped how fMRI data are interpreted. Later work extended the findings to alert monkeys and examined how different LFP frequency bands relate to haemodynamic responses.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Logothetis |first=Nikos K. |date=2008 |title=What we can do and what we cannot do with fMRI |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature06976 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=453 |issue=7197 |pages=869–878 |doi=10.1038/nature06976 |pmid=18548064 |bibcode=2008Natur.453..869L |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Logothetis conducted work on the neural basis of object recognition in macaque IT cortex, using carefully controlled, novel "paperclip" and wire-frame stimuli to examine how single neurons come to represent the shape and viewpoint of learned objects. This work provided some of the first single-cell evidence for view-dependent and view-invariant object representations in the ventral stream and supported view-based, rather than purely structural-description-based, theories of object recognition.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Logothetis |first1=Nikos K. |last2=Sheinberg |first2=David L. |date=1996-03-01 |title=Visual Object Recognition |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev.ne.19.030196.003045 |journal=Annual Review of Neuroscience |language=en |volume=19 |pages=577–621 |doi=10.1146/annurev.ne.19.030196.003045 |pmid=8833455 |issn=0147-006X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Animal rights controversy ==
In 2014, a German television station aired footage recorded in Logothetis's lab by an undercover representative of the German Animal Welfare Federation documenting violence and harm to animals that might attain the legal definition of a regulation violation for [[Animal testing on non-human primates|primates]]. Logothetis announced in response that he would no longer work with non-human primates in 2015 due to lack of institutional support and protection for his research program. [[Police raid]]s and investigations at this time did not find evidence of animal regulation violations.<ref name=sci20/>

Formal charges were brought against Logothetis and two staff members in August 2017 for allegedly delaying euthanasia to sick animals. On 20 February 2018, the Tübingen district court issued all three scientists a "penalty order," consisting of a fine and a sentence that would be automatically transformed into a conviction, which Logothetis immediately appealed. Following the order's announcement, the [[Max Planck Society]] (MPS) removed Logothetis's animal research responsibilities and right to conduct animal experiments.

Logothetis garnered significant support from members of the scientific community who criticized the MPS's decision to impose sanctions on Logothetis before a verdict had been reached regarding the alleged misconduct.<ref name=nat18a>{{cite journal |title=Max Planck scientists criticize handling of animal-rights charges against leading neuroscientist |date=2018-05-30 |last=Abbott |first=Alison |journal=Nature |volume=588 |issue=7708 |pages=13–14 |pmid=29872188 |doi=10.1038/d41586-018-05187-w |bibcode=2018Natur.558...13A |s2cid=46946752 |doi-access=free }}</ref> The [[Society for Neuroscience]] (SfN) and [[Federation of European Neuroscience Societies]] (FENS) issued a joint statement in his support,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fens.org/News-Activities/News/20181/08/FENS-SfN-Joint-Statement-on-Prof-Logothetis/ |title=FENS and SfN statement in strong support of Prof. Logothetis |website=FENS (Federation of European Neuroscience Societies) |date=2018-08-03 |access-date=2020-01-27}}</ref> followed by the [[International Brain Research Organization]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ibro.org/statement-logothetis/ |title=IBRO Statement in Support of Professor Nikos K. Logothetis |date=2018-08-10 |author1=Pierre Magistretti |author2=Keiji Tanaka |author3=Hans-Joachim Pflüger |author4=Pierre Luabeya |author5=Bong-Kiun Kaang |author6=Robert Gabriel |author7=Cecilia Bouzat |author8=Samuel David |access-date=2020-01-27}}</ref>

The specific charges Logothetis appealed were dismissed on 19 December 2018.<ref name=nat18b>{{cite journal |title=German court dismisses animal-welfare case against leading neuroscientist |date=2018-05-30 |last=Abbott |first=Aligermson |journal=Nature |doi=10.1038/d41586-018-07868-y |s2cid=150323898 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-018-07868-y |access-date=2020-01-27|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Subsequently, the MPS restored Logothetis's duties at the Institute for Biological Cybernetics.<ref name=nat19>{{cite journal|last=Abbott |first=Alison |title=Max Planck Society returns duties to leading neuroscientist after animal-welfare row |journal=Nature |date=2019-01-08 |doi=10.1088/1361-648X/aad6f1 |pmid=30061475 |arxiv=1805.10220 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-019-00047-7 |access-date=2020-01-27 |volume=30 |issue=36 |page=364001|s2cid=51867379 }}</ref>

Influenced by continued skepticism and lack of support for animal research in Germany, Logothetis announced in 2020 that he would move his department to the International Center for Primate Brain Research in [[Shanghai]] and co-direct the center with Chinese neuroscientist [[Mu-ming Poo]] by late 2020 or early 2021.<ref name=sci20/>

== Awards and honours ==

* 1999 Golden Brain Award, Minerva Foundation, [[University of California, Berkeley]]
* 2003 [[Louis-Jeantet Prize|Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]]
* 2004 Klaus Joachim Zülch Prize, Max Planck Society
* 2005 Elected member, [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]
* 2008 [[W. Alden Spencer Award]]
* 2022–2024 Research.com Neuroscience in China Leader Award
* 2024 Vyzov Prize for Future Technologies (Discovery category) – first non-Russian recipient of the award, for his contributions to the development of fMRI and its application to studying human brain activity<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-20 |title=US-based scientist Valery Fokin wins Vyzov Prize, beating fierce Chinese rivals |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3337128/us-based-scientist-valery-fokin-wins-vyzov-prize-beating-fierce-chinese-rivals |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}}</ref>
* 2025 International Cooperation Award of the Chinese Academy of Sciences
* 2025 Academician of the World Academy for Artificial Consciousness<ref>{{Cite web |last=Editorial |first=WAAC |title=WAAC |url=https://www.waac.ac/ |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=World Academy for Artificial Consciousness |language=en}}</ref>
